title: How Git Actually Stores Things: Objects, Refs, and HEAD
intro: Most Git confusion disappears once you know the model: a commit is a snapshot (not a diff), a branch is just a file holding one commit id, and nothing you commit is truly lost for weeks. Five commands show you the whole thing. The CI/CD category covers the everyday flow; this one goes underneath it.

steps.prompt: Find the full commit id that HEAD currently points to.
steps.why: rev-parse turns any name (HEAD, main, v1.2.0, HEAD~3) into the object id it stands for. Scripts should use it instead of parsing 'git log' output, which is meant for people.

steps.fake_output:
tree 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904
parent 3e1f0a9c5d7b2e4f6a8c0e1d3f5b7a9c1e2d4f60
author Alice <alice@example.com> 1790000000 +0000
committer Alice <alice@example.com> 1790000000 +0000

Add rate limiting to the API
steps.explanation: A commit is four things: a tree (the full snapshot), its parent commit(s), who and when, and a message.
steps.why: A commit points at a complete snapshot of the project (the tree), not at a set of changes. Diffs are computed on demand by comparing two snapshots. That's why switching branches is fast, and why history is a chain: each commit names its parent.

steps.prompt: List what's in the snapshot: the tree of HEAD.
steps.fake_output:
100644 blob 8c7e5a667f1b771847fe88c01c3de34413a1b220	README.md
100755 blob 1f7a7a472abf3dd9643fd615f6da379c4acb3e3a	deploy.sh
040000 tree 2d1c0b9a8f7e6d5c4b3a29181716151413121110	src
steps.explanation: Blobs are file contents, trees are directories, and the mode records whether a file is executable.
steps.why: A blob's id is the hash of its content, so two identical files, in any commit or branch, are stored once. That's why Git repositories stay small despite storing a full snapshot per commit.

steps.prompt: See what a branch really is: list every ref and the commit it points to.
steps.explanation: Each branch and tag is one line: a name and a commit id.
steps.why: A branch is a 41-byte file, which is why creating one is instant and free. 'Deleting a branch' deletes the name, not the commits. And 'origin/main' is just your local record of where main was the last time you fetched.

steps.prompt: Check how much space the object database uses, in human-readable units.
steps.fake_output:
count: 312
size: 1.42 MiB
in-pack: 48211
packs: 3
size-pack: 86.31 MiB
prune-packable: 0
garbage: 0
steps.explanation: 312 loose objects, and 48,211 compressed into packfiles totalling 86 MiB.
steps.why: New objects start 'loose' (one file each) and are later packed and delta-compressed by 'git gc'. A repository that's unexpectedly huge usually has large binaries in its history, which packing can't shrink. git-incident-003 deals with exactly that.
